policies.summary: Every wind or solar facility over 0.5 MW needs a permit from the board of county commissioners; in addition, wind facilities of 20 or more turbines and solar facilities over 30 MW or disturbing 100 acres or more need an Industrial Siting Council permit, and a county may refer a smaller project to the Council.

Counties may not permit a wind turbine closer than 110 percent of tower height to adjoining property lines and public roads, 5.5 times tower height (at least 1,000 feet) to a dwelling or platted subdivision, or half a mile to a city or town limit, or within two nautical miles of an active military missile launch or control facility without military and FAA clearances; solar arrays must stay 300 feet from occupied structures, 100 feet inside the facility boundary and 100 to 200 feet from roads, though counties may vary the solar setbacks. County rules may not be less stringent for wind.

projects.description: In 2011, Wasatch Wind proposed a 66-turbine wind farm in Converse County.
The Rail Tie Wind Project, a 26,000-acre, 504-MW wind farm proposed by ConnectGen (which was acquired by Repsol in March 2024), has experienced delays after becoming embroiled in legal controversies.

In July 2023, a conservation group in Wyoming called the Albany County Conservancy challenged the Bureau of Land Management’s approval of a transmission line designed to connect a proposed wind project to interstate transmission lines.
EG Haystack Solar LLC proposed the 199-MW Haystack Solar and battery energy storage facility on a 2,000-acre private ranch 30 miles west of Casper.
In 2018, Repsol Renewables North America began the development of the 650-MW Laramie Range Wind Project, comprising 170 wind turbines on approximately 56,000 acres 20 miles northwest of Cheyenne.
In 2022, Focus Clean Energy proposed the “Pronghorn H2” project, comprising a roughly 300 MW wind farm and 280 MW solar farm, to power a hydrogen production facility.
In 2025, Focus Clean Energy, Acciona, and Nordex Green Hydrogen jointly proposed the 1,000-MW Sidewinder H2 Wind farm on approximately 120,000 acres of private and public land in eastern Wyoming.
